title: Geometrical Sensitivity Analysis and Optimization of PEM Water Electrolyzers: An Integrated Thermo-Electrochemical and Machine Learning Approach
content: This study presents an integrated numerical framework combining diffusion aware thermo-electrochemical modeling, geometrical sensitivity analysis, machine learning, and genetic algorithm optimization to improve proton exchange membrane water electrolyzers (PEMWE) performance under fixed operating conditions. Fourteen geometrical parameters were investigated using a dataset of 10000 configurations generated through Latin hypercube sampling. One factor at a time analysis, normalized local sensitivity, and Pearson and Spearman correlation analyses were employed to identify the dominant geometrical effects. An artificial neural network (ANN) was subsequently developed to predict cell voltage, energy efficiency, exergy efficiency, and specific energy consumption (SEC), while SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) were used to interpret the model predictions and prioritize influential design variables. The results identify membrane thickness as the dominant geometrical parameter, with increasing thickness from 50 to 200 µm producing a voltage increase of 111.6 mV and an SEC increase of 2.967 kWh.kg-1. The ANN achieved test set coefficients of determination exceeding 0.99998 for all four performance indicators. Based on the SHAP analysis, five geometrical parameters were selected for single objective genetic algorithm optimization. Re6evaluation of the optimized configuration using the physics based model demonstrated a reduction in cell voltage from 2.317825 to 2.296674 V (0.9125%), accompanied by a decrease in SEC from 61.6292 to 61.0668 kWh.kg⁻¹ and improvements in energy and exergy efficiencies.
